- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak or adjust downward by 5–10% if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.36) and forecast is below recent history mean, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with sentiment momentum.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent high; cap at 10% above 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 3–7% to match true price decay.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.44) and forecast is low, model underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.18–0.53), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before applying correction.
